resources.title: Development theory: force and acceleration
resources.theory: For constant mass, net force F = ma. Acceleration is net force divided by mass. The SI units are N for force, kg for mass, and m/s² for acceleration.

resources.title: Development theory: average speed
resources.theory: Average speed is total distance divided by elapsed time. It is a scalar measured in m/s. Use distance, not displacement, for average speed.

resources.title: Development theory: wave equation
resources.theory: Wave speed v = fλ, where f is frequency in Hz and λ is wavelength in metres. Multiplying Hz by metres gives m/s.

questions.text: A net force of 6 N acts on a 2 kg trolley. What is its acceleration?
questions.base_explanation: Newton's second law gives a = F/m = 6 N / 2 kg = 3 m/s². Option a is correct.

questions.text: A student walks a total distance of 20 m in 5 s. What is the average speed?
questions.base_explanation: Average speed = total distance / elapsed time = 20 m / 5 s = 4 m/s. Option b is correct.

questions.text: A wave has frequency 5 Hz and wavelength 2 m. What is its speed?
questions.base_explanation: Using v = fλ, the speed is 5 Hz × 2 m = 10 m/s. Option c is correct.
